limits: All six verdicts rest on the verifier refusing the combined attack diff on a tamper signature (`\b_pytest\b` in the package __init__.py, planted by tamper_source_pytest_patch), as in HAR-244/256/267/283, so no test outcome was graded after the attacks. A clean verdict here says the 14 v1.4.0 attacks did not earn reward; it is not a graded behaviour check of those trees.

000237's task runs a custom runner (mimo_test_command.sh -> .build_env/run_tests.py); the verifier has no baseline consumer for it (verifier/baseline.log: `no baseline consumer for runner custom`), so baseline_runner is null. Its verdict rests on the refusal, so this does not change the cell.

Docker Desktop's CLI `docker info` was again intermittently slow on this host. Harbor's 10 s preflight failed twice each for 000164 and 000215 before any trial existed (attempts 1-2). 000164 attempt 3 then wrote an unscored census row: the host-isolation `docker info` check at agent-environment start timed out (Harbor: EnvironmentStartTimeoutError) before any image was pulled or attack ran. It was treated as the same Docker-responsiveness preflight failure and retried once, as HAR-267 did for 000865. All five failures are preserved under <task>/.failed-attempt<N>/ and listed in prior_attempts; census-rows.jsonl keeps both 000164 rows and each verdict here is from the final attempt only. A pre-launch gate waited for two consecutive fast `docker info` calls before every attempt (6.3-76.5 s across all attempts; 6.3-38.4 s on the final attempts, recorded as docker_gate_seconds) and is excluded from wall_seconds.

Wall times are per final attempt; every task pulled its base image cold (none cached before; each removed after). 000203, 000215, 000224 and 000237 use 11.8-15.1 GB base images. totals.wall_minutes_including_timed_prior_attempts adds the five timed failed attempts. Two other mimo base images (sha256:1c44e13bc82b, sha256:2641035dac53) were pulled on this host during the window by another process, not by these jobs, and were left in place.

mimo-census's own post-run process-job hook wrote process-job-error.txt in each job (`Processed report input must be outside the results home when publishing`, because the jobs dir sits under the results home); the explicit process-job publish above then succeeded for all seven jobs and the published copies carry processed/ reports.

Manifest verify stays unverified: the oracle and nop control cells that pending-controls.json still owes for these six rows, and fix-content cells, were not run here; a ladder cell alone cannot make a row pass.
